fixtures.label: Two orders, one organization — the delivery leg
fixtures.description:
The family's FIRST fixture, covering what the family exists for: a CROSS-ORDER sheet. Two orders (964, 1020) under one organization, two destinations, 13 units — no per-order document can express this. Scope `organization:...:all:delivery` also pins the `<kind>:<uid>:<gate>:<leg>` grammar (api-cloudrun#824) on its `organization` arm.

1. THE GROUP HEADINGS. Three group dividers across the two orders (`Carts & Ramps`, `Traffic, Safety & Signage`, `Crafty`) — what `buildPackingListForLeg` (core#80, beta.326) exists to keep. The bug it fixed was SILENT: `groupByDestination` strips dividers while `buildPackingList` derives `group_name` by walking for the last `group` row it passed, so composing them returned null for every heading. The grid still rendered and the headings a picker navigates by were absent. Only a rendered sheet catches it, so this fixture is the gate.

2. RENTAL AND SALE TOGETHER — the delivery leg's defining property. 964 is three rentals, 1020 a `sale` (8 cases of water). Delivery admits both; collection is rental only, because a sale does not come back. A collection-leg fixture is NOT a near-duplicate and must be added separately.

3. A COMPLETE DOCUMENT. `order_count` is 2 and the fold returns 2 with `next_cursor: null`, so `orders.length === order_count` holds — the template REFUSES a short document, and only a fixture satisfying it exercises that.

Also carries real SHORTAGES (all three of 964's bookings short by 1 against a `reserved` breakdown) and `stores: []` on `Driving Sign Kit`, the no-stock-record arm.

Deliberately SMALL so the golden reads in one view. The 17-order sheet at destination `3100 W Fillmore St` is the page-break case and belongs in its own fixture.

KNOWN ARTIFACT, do not "repair": `scope.name`, `orders[].subject` and `destinations[].name` render as masked filler — all three are `pii: "mask"` as of beta.324/.326/.328. The give-back is legibility only (api-cloudrun#837).
